title: Flat quasi-compact relation images as intersections of quasi-compact opens
statement: Let $R,V$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $V$ quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $s,t:R\to V$ be flat quasi-compact morphisms [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every quasi-compact open subset $H\subseteq|V|$ [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], put $E=t(s^{-1}(H))$. Then $E$ is quasi-compact in the induced topology and is closed under generalization: if $y\in E$ and $y\in\overline{\{y'\}}$, then $y'\in E$. There exists a quasi-compact open $H_2\subseteq V$ containing $E$. For every such $H_2$, the set $\mathcal U=\{U\subseteq H_2:U\text{ is open and quasi-compact, and }E\subseteq U\}$ is nonempty and $E=\bigcap_{U\in\mathcal U}U$. Each member of $\mathcal U$ is also a quasi-compact open subset of $V$, so the displayed equality is an intersection of a nonempty set-indexed family of quasi-compact opens of $V$. No equivalence relation or invariance hypothesis on $s,t$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0APA (lemma-first-observation), proof: quasi-compact generalization-stable image, containing quasi-compact open and spectral intersection argument. The proof uses no groupoid law.

proof.text: Put $A=s^{-1}(H)$, an open subset of $R$ by continuity. Cover $H$ by affine opens contained in $H$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Quasi-compactness of $H$ gives a finite subcover $H=H_1\cup\cdots\cup H_n$. By the definition in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], every $s^{-1}(H_i)$ is quasi-compact. Their finite union $A$ is quasi-compact: restrict an open cover to each of these finitely many sets and combine its finite subcovers. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact] to the continuous restriction $t|_A:A\to V$. Its image is $E$, so $E$ is quasi-compact in the induced topology.

Let $y=t(r)\in E$, with $r\in A$, and let $y\in\overline{\{y\prime\}}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] to the flat morphism $t$: there is $r\prime$ with $r\in\overline{\{r\prime\}}$ and $t(r\prime)=y\prime$. Since $A$ is open and contains $r$, its being an open neighbourhood of $r\in\overline{\{r\prime\}}$ forces $r\prime\in A$. Thus $y\prime\in E$. This proves generalization stability without using any groupoid identity.

By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose affine open neighbourhoods in $V$ of the points of $E$. They are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Compactness of $E$ supplies finitely many of them covering $E$. Their union is a quasi-compact open $H_2$ of $V$: for an open cover of this union, take a finite subcover on each of the finitely many affine opens. If $E=\varnothing$, the empty union gives $H_2=\varnothing$.

Fix any quasi-compact open $H_2$ containing $E$. The open subscheme $H_2$ is quasi-separated: cover it by affine opens using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; these are affine opens of $V$, so their pairwise intersections are quasi-compact by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion] for $V$. Clause (2) of that node applied to this cover gives quasi-separatedness of $H_2$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral] makes $H_2$ spectral. The subspace topology on $E$ induced from $H_2$ is the one induced from $V$, so $E$ is still quasi-compact.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-generalizations-of-quasi-compact] in $H_2$ to $E$. The set $W=\{x\in H_2:\overline{\{x\}}^{H_2}\cap E\ne\varnothing\}$ equals the intersection of all quasi-compact opens of $H_2$ containing $E$. Here $W=E$: reflexivity gives $E\subseteq W$, while if $e\in E\cap\overline{\{x\}}^{H_2}$ then $e\in\overline{\{x\}}^V$, and step 2 gives $x\in E$. Thus $E=\bigcap_{U\in\mathcal U}U$ inside $H_2$. The family $\mathcal U$ is a set, being a subfamily of the power set of $|H_2|$, and is nonempty since it contains $H_2$ itself. Every member is open in $V$ because $H_2$ is open, and is quasi-compact in $V$ because the induced topology on it is unchanged. Nonemptiness ensures the same intersection taken inside $V$ has no extra point outside $H_2$. This proves every clause, including the empty case, using no equivalence relation or invariance property.
